Ella está esperando desde las nueve.

Pregunta

head: Uso
Ejemplo
Español
rows: Algo que empezó hace un tiempo y sigue
I've been learning English for three years.
Llevo tres años estudiando inglés.
¿Cuánto tiempo?
How long have you been living here?
¿Cuánto tiempo llevas viviendo aquí?
Efecto visible de algo reciente

blocks.title: Llevo una hora esperando
blocks.text: El español dice Llevo una hora esperando, Hace una hora que espero o Espero desde hace una hora. El inglés nunca usa el presente para esto. Di I've been waiting for an hour. I'm waiting since an hour o I wait from one hour son errores típicos de los hispanohablantes.

head: Present perfect simple
Present perfect continuous
rows: El resultado, la cantidad: I've read three books this month.
La actividad, la duración: I've been reading all afternoon.
Terminado: I've painted the kitchen. (ya está acabada)
En curso, quizá sin terminar: I've been painting the kitchen. (tengo pintura en las manos)
Permanente: I've lived here all my life.
Temporal: I've been living with friends since May.
Con los estados: I've known him for years.
No con los estados: I've been knowing him (incorrecto).

blocks.title: How many / how much: simple
blocks.text: Si preguntas por una cantidad, usa el simple: How many cups of coffee have you had? Si preguntas por la duración, el continuous: How long have you been drinking coffee?

blocks.title: Verbos de estado
blocks.text: know, like, love, believe, own, be y otros verbos de estado no van en continuous: I've known her since school (la conozco desde el colegio), We've been married for ten years (llevamos diez años casados).

rows: I wait here since ten o'clock.
I've been waiting here since ten o'clock.
Algo en curso hasta ahora: present perfect continuous.
I'm learning English for two years.
I've been learning English for two years.
Duración hasta ahora: no el present continuous.
She has been knowing him for years.
She has known him for years.
know no va en continuous.
How long are you living here?
How long have you been living here?
Cuánto tiempo llevas: present perfect continuous.
I've been reading three books.
I've read three books.
Una cantidad: present perfect simple.
He has been work all day.
He has been working all day.
Después de been va la forma en -ing.
We have been waiting since two hours.
We have been waiting for two hours.
Un periodo: for.

blocks.text: Completa con el present perfect simple o continuous. Las respuestas están en la última página.

items.q: I ______ for you for twenty minutes!
items.full: I have been waiting for you for twenty minutes!

items.q: How long ______ you been learning English?
items.full: How long have you been learning English?

items.q: She ______ all morning. She looks tired.
items.full: She has been working all morning. She looks tired.
I have written four emails today.

items.q: We ______ each other since we were children.
items.full: We have known each other since we were children.
It has been raining since this morning.

items.q: Your hands are dirty. What have you ______ doing?
items.full: Your hands are dirty. What have you been doing?

items.q: They ______ living in Leeds for six months.
items.full: They have been living in Leeds for six months.

items.q: He's been playing the guitar ______ ten years.
items.full: He's been playing the guitar for ten years.

items.q: How many cups of tea ______ you had today?
items.full: How many cups of tea have you had today?

items.q: I ______ my keys. I can't find them anywhere.
items.full: I have lost my keys. I can't find them anywhere.

items.a: I've been waiting for an hour.
How long have you been living here?
It has been raining all day.

items.q: La conozco desde hace diez años.
items.a: I have known her for ten years.
